final_candidates.decision_summary: Replaces a critical core tryptophan residue with a charged glutamate, severely disrupting hydrophobic packing and destabilizing fold.
Introduces a charged glutamate residue into an aromatic core position, impairing structural stability and causing protein unfolding.
Disrupts hydrophobic interactions at position 48 by substituting phenylalanine with glutamate, promoting loss of tertiary structure.

stop_reason.detail: Top candidates adequately cover the primary objective of disrupting protein folding via strategic hydrophobic core mutations.

history.rationale: Substituting the conserved core aromatic tryptophan at position 17 with a charged glutamate creates a severe desolvation penalty. This uncompensated charge in the hydrophobic core will disrupt tertiary packing and destabilize PsaE folding.
Strong candidate targeting a key aromatic residue to destabilize hydrophobic core packing.

Replacing buried aromatic phenylalanine 40 with a negatively charged glutamate residue introduces electrostatic repulsion and desolvation penalties in the hydrophobic core. This significantly destabilizes protein folding and structure.
Introduces a charged glutamate at a bulky aromatic site to disrupt core stability.
Introducing a charged glutamate residue into core aromatic position 48 perturbs hydrophobic core packing. The energetic cost of burying a charge destabilizes the folded conformation.
Disrupts local hydrophobic interactions in key structural region.

Mutating core hydrophobic leucine 11 to proline introduces backbone conformational constraints and removes hydrophobic side-chain contacts. This disrupts local secondary structure and destabilizes protein folding.
Proline introduction breaks local secondary structure backbone.
Replacing hydrophobic aromatic phenylalanine 60 near the C-terminus with glutamate causes significant core charge burial. This destabilizes the native fold and disrupts PsaE assembly.
Targeting C-terminal hydrophobic packing to induce unfolding.
Inserting a charged glutamate at hydrophobic core position 33 perturbs interior packing and introduces electrostatic destabilization. This strongly disfavors the native folded state.
Charge introduction at hydrophobic isoleucine destabilizes fold.
Mutating core leucine 65 to a negatively charged glutamate disrupts hydrophobic interactions in the C-terminal region. Burial of charge severely destabilizes protein fold stability.
Glutamate substitution impairs terminal hydrophobic core stability.
Replacing core aromatic tyrosine 18 with negatively charged aspartate disrupts aromatic hydrophobic packing. The charge burial penalty causes substantial destabilization of PsaE folding.
Aspartate substitution disrupts aromatic stacking interactions.
Substituting buried hydrophobic valine 38 with charged glutamate introduces adverse core electrostatic interactions. This significantly reduces folding free energy and destabilizes the protein.
Valine to glutamate mutation reduces overall fold stability.
Inserting a proline residue at position 34 interrupts local backbone geometry and disrupts hydrophobic packing of tyrosine 34. This structural perturbation destabilizes the native tertiary fold.
Proline substitution severely distorts backbone conformation.
